transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Thursday, November 12. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Complete data could've raised average Delhi Diwali pollution level by 49 percent. On Diwali night, the absence of PM2.5 data from monitoring stations led to distorted pollution readings in Delhi. Research by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air indicated that pollution levels might have increased by as much as 49 percent . While the Central Pollution Control Board pointed out calibration limitations, readings from the Delhi Pollution Control Committee were inconsistent. Meta's infrastructure chief Santosh Janardhan quits after 15 years. In a significant move, Santosh Janardhan will relinquish his leadership position at Meta by early 2027, paving the way for David Brown, who joined from AWS in July, to take the helm. Janardhan will provide guidance during Brown's transition to ensure a smooth handover. This strategic shift is part of Meta's ongoing effort to enhance its data center operations and bolster investments in artificial intelligence and related infrastructure. Chased and then shot: Chilling CCTV video of ex-Tech Mahindra regional head's murder. CCTV footage captured the events leading to the murder of Paramjeet Dhankhar by his neighbour, Mohan Sharma. An argument lasting four minutes escalated, resulting in Sharma shooting Dhankhar multiple times. Despite attempts to escape, Dhankhar was pursued and fired upon even after collapsing. Investigations indicate a long-standing dispute over parking may have sparked the incident. IIT-BHU grad's project helps 50,000 farmers earn from solar power. Bhavesh Patidar, hailing from a traditional farming lineage, established SolarSure with a vision to support farmers through solar energy initiatives. By equipping over 50,000 farmers with solar installations across various states, the company is creating alternative revenue streams beyond conventional farming. Utilizing advanced technology, SolarSure evaluates land for optimal solar performance, aiming to bolster the financial stability of farming families throughout India. 'Mumbai were keen on Arshdeep': Ness Wadia reveals how Hardik trade materialised. Punjab Kings co-owner Ness Wadia opens up about the blockbuster Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade, admitting that letting go of the India pacer was a difficult decision. Wadia explains the cricketing rationale behind acquiring Pandya, reveals how the negotiations unfolded and outlines the franchise's long-term ambitions of building a championship-winning team. Watch: US war secretary Pete Hegseth reprimanded by soldier at Arlington Cemetery. US secretary of war Pete Hegseth was publicly reprimanded by a US Army soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery after members of his entourage were seen laughing and talking near the memorial following a Veterans Day ceremony. 'I'd tape it to my thumb': Ex-Australia star admits to using sandpaper. Stuart MacGill has acknowledged using sandpaper on the ball during his cricket career, indicating it was not a deliberate cheating strategy. His admission follows recent statements made by Usman Khawaja in his memoir, which has reopened discussions on Sandpapergate. Cricket Australia maintains that the wider team was unaware of any wrongdoing during the 2018 Cape Town Test. Could Jensen Huang join Elon Musk? Tesla CEO responds to hiring suggestion. Tech billionaire Elon Musk on Thursday weighed in on the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose extramarital relationship with Megaspeed International founder Alice Huang have triggered questions over possible links to Chinese intelligence. Judge 'close to' CJI runs transfer risk once mentor leaves office. The Supreme Court collegium is working to establish a systematic policy for transferring judges among high courts. Currently, transfers are largely subject to personal criteria, which the collegium aims to revise. This new policy emphasizes objective reasoning to streamline the transfer process, reduce personal biases, and enhance accountability regarding judges' conduct and expertise, marking a pivotal evolution in judicial integrity management. Louisiana father's will challenged by six children; court orders fresh hearings. A contentious family feud arose when six of a father's nine children contested the legitimacy of his will, arguing discrepancies in signatures and the execution process. However, after legal deliberations, an appeals court overturned the initial ruling that declared the will invalid, citing insufficient evidence from the challengers. This ruling paves the way for the succession process to proceed under fresh legal stipulations. Jensen Huang had another affair with Nvidia VP who reported to him: Report. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who is already facing scrutiny over his alleged extramarital relationship with a Chinese businesswoman identified by US intelligence officials as a suspected Chinese spy, was also involved in another affair with a senior company executive, according to a report by The New York Times. Kentucky dad removed from sons' baseball game; court revives defamation claim. John Carroll's experience at a high school baseball game led to a lengthy legal dispute over defamation. After being escorted out following a verbal altercation involving his son, Carroll filed a lawsuit. The Kentucky Court of Appeals revived his defamation claim against former athletic director Charlotte Marshall. Carroll's claims regarding interference with his career were dismissed because he secured a promotion shortly afterward.
